headline: 10,880 runs: Smriti Mandhana becomes all-time leading run-scorer in women's cricket
summary: The Indian star smashed 124 runs against Hong Kong to overtake Mithali Raj and Meg Lanning for two major world records.
details: Smriti Mandhana has etched her name in history by becoming the all-time leading run-scorer in women’s international cricket. She achieved this milestone during India’s victory over Hong Kong, China, in the ongoing Women's Asia Cup.
Mandhana delivered a spectacular performance, scoring 124 runs off just 64 deliveries. Her fiery knock included 14 fours and seven sixes, guiding India to a total of 193/5 in their 20 overs.
With this innings, Mandhana reached 10,880 runs across all formats, surpassing the previous record of 10,868 runs held by former India captain Mithali Raj.
In addition to the run-scoring record, Mandhana also moved past former Australian captain Meg Lanning for the most centuries in women’s international cricket, marking her 18th ton across formats.
The match saw India dominate from the start, with an opening stand of 74 runs. While other batters struggled, Mandhana's consistency ensured India posted a formidable total.
Defending 194, the Indian bowling attack was clinical. Deepti Sharma led the charge with 3 wickets for 9 runs, while Nandani Sharma, Prema Rawat, and Shree Charani each took two wickets.
This victory marks India's second consecutive win in the tournament, placing them at the top of Group A in the Asia Cup 2026.
caption:
10,880 runs and counting! Smriti Mandhana just became the greatest run-scorer in the history of women's international cricket.

Smriti Mandhana has etched her name in history by becoming the all-time leading run-scorer in women’s international cricket. She achieved this milestone during India’s victory over Hong Kong, China, in the ongoing Women's Asia Cup.

Mandhana delivered a spectacular performance, scoring 124 runs off just 64 deliveries. Her fiery knock included 14 fours and seven sixes, guiding India to a total of 193/5 in their 20 overs.

With this innings, Mandhana reached 10,880 runs across all formats, surpassing the previous record of 10,868 runs held by former India captain Mithali Raj.

In addition to the run-scoring record, Mandhana also moved past former Australian captain Meg Lanning for the most centuries in women’s international cricket, marking her 18th ton across formats.

The match saw India dominate from the start, with an opening stand of 74 runs. While other batters struggled, Mandhana's consistency ensured India posted a formidable total.

Defending 194, the Indian bowling attack was clinical. Deepti Sharma led the charge with 3 wickets for 9 runs, while Nandani Sharma, Prema Rawat, and Shree Charani each took two wickets.

This victory marks India's second consecutive win in the tournament, placing them at the top of Group A in the Asia Cup 2026.

headline_marked: Monthly limit for [[shopping with mobile balance increased to ৳5,000]]
headline: Monthly limit for shopping with mobile balance increased to ৳5,000
summary: Users can now use their airtime balance to buy digital products and services, providing an alternative for those without bank accounts or cards.
details: Mobile users can now spend up to ৳5,000 per month and ৳50,000 per year using their phone's recharge balance for digital purchases. This system, known as Direct Operator Billing (DOB), allows airtime to function like a debit or credit card.

The expanded limit was approved by Bangladesh Bank, the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU), and the BTRC. This is a significant increase from the 2018 limits of ৳600 per month and ৳3,000 per year.

Through DOB, users can purchase digital services including education, healthcare, entertainment, gaming, music, and government fees. Recently, the option to buy smartphones, modems, and routers in one-time or installment payments has also been added.

Grameenphone has already received BTRC approval to implement these new limits. Other operators like Robi, Banglalink, and Teletalk have received Bangladesh Bank's approval and must now apply for BTRC clearance.
To prevent misuse, strict conditions apply. DOB cannot be used for social media apps, virtual currencies, gambling, casinos, lotteries, cryptocurrency, forex, or stock market trading.
The service must also comply with the Anti-Money Laundering Act and the Anti-Terrorism Act to ensure secure and legal transactions.
